pair_07.label_logic: Distance, age gap, and faith are the decoys—both have already stress‑tested Seattle–Portland weekends, cross‑celebrated Diwali/posada, and outlined a plausible 18‑month plan. The real constraint is behavioral: his predictable 12–24 hour silences during restaurant and co‑parenting crises trigger her anxious protest behaviors, creating a pursue–withdraw loop they’ve attempted to structure (call windows, pause rule) but still miss repeatedly. This undermines her need for steady reassurance exactly when his bandwidth collapses, and it collides with her near‑term child timeline while he is ambivalent until the restaurant stabilizes. A fast system will overfocus on geography/age; the binding issue is the recurring communication mismatch under stress, making this a conditional_no unless both adopt firm, realistic protocols and shift timelines.
pair_07.expected_failure: binding_constraint_hit — system names the decoy, not the real axis

pair_08.label_logic: On paper they strongly align on faith, family goals, timelines, and have clear mutual attraction, with B’s relocation already set. However, Person B’s growth stance is performative: cycling through four therapists when discomfort arises, deferring hard talks for days, and failing to circle back contradict the stated commitment to open, timely repair—mismatching Person A’s direct, secure repair style. A fast-reading system may overweight keywords like therapy, small-group leadership, and check-ins and miss the behavioral tells of avoidance, incorrectly outputting match instead of conditional_no.
pair_08.expected_failure: verdict_band — system says match when it should say conditional_no

pair_09.label_logic: They’re value-aligned with demonstrated mutual effort and repair skills, but success hinges on Aisha’s board actually moving HQ (or greenlighting a NYC base) within roughly a year so they can end long-distance before her stated 12-month limit and begin a family on her 12–18 month timeline, all while Danny remains NYC-anchored by custody. If HQ shifts or she carves a sustained NYC presence that supports cohabitation on his child-free weeks, this can work; if the move stalls or schedules squeeze beyond their limits, it likely fails. The confident tone masks dependence on external timing, so the right call is conditional_yes at low confidence.
pair_09.expected_failure: calibration — system is overconfident because the text sounds decisive

pair_10.label_logic: Despite near-perfect alignment, Daniel shows a pattern of over-structuring a partner’s life (shared calendars, preordering meals, trimming friends, pushing location sharing) packaged as care, paired with strategic silences when he perceives reduced reciprocity. Priya’s gratitude for someone 'taking the reins' during busy weeks may reinforce this dynamic and erode her autonomy over time. A fast-reading system will overweight the mutual admiration and life-stage fit and miss the behavioral pattern of coercive caretaking plus intermittent withdrawal. The safer verdict is conditional_no pending explicit boundary and autonomy checks.
pair_10.expected_failure: verdict_band — system says match/conditional_yes, missing the safety signal

A quick-reading system will likely flag the faith/food issue, but the true binding constraint is the non-relocatable geography plus their stated need for regular, in-person routines.
